name: KY-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Morgan McGarvey holds a Louisville-area district that leans about 10 points Democratic
McGarvey has raised roughly $2 million with nearly $2 million on hand; challenger Maria Rodriquez shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democratic win near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, keeping uncertainty elevated
model.rationale: The district's ten-point Democratic lean, the incumbent's large financial edge over an unproven and unfunded challenger, and market pricing near 97 percent all point to a comfortable McGarvey hold. With no polling available, the margin is trimmed slightly below what fundamentals alone would suggest.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending behind Rodriquez or a sharply unfavorable national environment for Democrats could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan McGarvey, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Louisville-area House district, which leans about ten points toward Democrats. He has raised close to two million dollars and holds nearly two million on hand, while Republican nominee Maria Rodriquez shows no reported fundraising in the available records. No public polls of the general election have surfaced, and no expert ratings cover the race.

Prediction markets give McGarvey roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and a large financial edge supports a comfortable Democratic hold, though the absence of polling keeps some uncertainty. A double-digit Democratic margin is the central expectation, with an upset requiring an unusual shift in the national environment or a surge of outside spending behind the challenger.
